prompt: Complete Calculator: add() and multiply() return Operation lambdas, and calculate runs any Operation on two ints.
explanation: Operation has exactly one abstract method, which makes it a functional interface, so a lambda like (a, b) -> a + b can implement it without any named class. add() and multiply() return those lambdas as values, and calculate shows the flip side: code that accepts behavior and invokes it through op.apply(a, b). Separating the choice of operation from its execution is the core idea behind programming with lambdas.
hints: Operation has a single abstract method, so a lambda of shape (a, b) -> ... can implement it.
add() and multiply() should each return such a lambda directly -- no new class, no anonymous class.
calculate just forwards its two ints to op.apply and returns the result.
